routines.semantics: Test a signed32 zero-based permutation. Positive-length bijections return true. Empty, repeated, negative and out-of-range candidates return false, including INT_MAX.

scenarios.observes: Distinguish the canonical empty false result and the only one-element permutation.
Recognize identity, reverse order, multiple cycles and a long nonidentity cycle.
Reject even and odd multiplicities and repeated elements at either endpoint.
Observe false for negative, exactly one past the last and both signed32 extremes.
Exercise a nonconsecutive 31-element permutation, a missing index and restoration on the next call.

routines.edgeAssessment: Compare empty, singleton, fixed points, cycles, larger permutations, duplicate, negative and both signed32 extreme candidates. Independent direct predicate invocation maps the impossible INT_MAX to n before the canonical +1 conversion. Production substitutes −1 in a private copy.
routines.errorAssessment: Supported inputs have no routine-specific scientific failure case. A false order predicate or the ordinary short-array result is asserted as success. Wrapper range/type/resource errors are tested separately. Internal toolkit allocation failure can signal MALLOCFAILED; scientific resource exhaustion is not deliberately induced.
routines.fixtureRationale: Authored array, permutation and representation examples require no kernels or external files.
routines.cleanup: Both adapters snapshot data once and supply non-null physical storage for zero length. Native owns fixed typed buffers during its mutex-protected call. WASM releases each acquired buffer after success or failure and reads owned results only after the status check.

findings.summary: The pinned wrapper increments each input entry in a signed integer. INT_MAX is outside the supported index set, but directly incrementing it would overflow.
findings.repair: Replace that impossible value in private storage by an equivalent impossible sentinel before calling the real predicate. Independent code substitutes a different out-of-range index and checks the same false result.
